body.text: A federal judge has put Connecticut’s “convertible pistol” law on hold the day before it was due to take effect — the first court win against the new “Glock ban” laws.

On 30 September a federal judge enjoined Connecticut’s Public Act 26-41 hours before it took effect, finding the plaintiffs likely to win on Second Amendment grounds. Also corrected today: Johnson v. Jacobson is a carry-reciprocity case, and DOJ sued Minnesota on 24 September.
